lesson.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI

steps.title: Install FastAPI and create main.py
steps.instructions: Run pip install fastapi uvicorn in your terminal. Create a project folder, open it in VS Code, and create an empty main.py.

targets.caption: Create main.py in your project folder

explanations.topic: Why uvicorn is needed alongside FastAPI

hints: Have you installed both fastapi and the ASGI server uvicorn?
Run pip install fastapi and pip install uvicorn in your terminal, then create a new project folder.
Open the folder in VS Code and create an empty file named main.py.
common_mistakes: Installing fastapi without uvicorn, which is required to run the server.
Creating main.py outside the project directory opened in VS Code.

steps.title: Create root route and run server
steps.instructions: Import FastAPI, create an app instance, and add a GET '/' route returning {'Hello': 'World'} in main.py. Start the server with uvicorn main:app --reload and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in Chrome.

explanations.topic: How @app.get decorator defines a root path
What the --reload flag does in uvicorn

hints: How do you instantiate a FastAPI application and attach a GET handler to '/'?
Import FastAPI from fastapi, set app = FastAPI(), and decorate def root() with @app.get('/').
Run uvicorn main:app --reload in your terminal and visit http://127.0.0.1:8000.
common_mistakes: Running uvicorn from a different directory where main.py is not located.
Forgetting to save main.py before visiting the URL or omitting --reload.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: In main.py, initialize an empty items list and add a POST '/items' endpoint that appends an item string and returns the list. With uvicorn running, test it from a new terminal using curl.

targets.caption: Add the POST endpoint for items

explanations.topic: Query parameter handling in POST endpoint

hints: Where should you store created items in memory and which decorator handles POST requests?
Define items = [] at the top level, then add @app.post('/items') with def create_item(item: str):.
Append item to items, return items, and test with curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post for creating items.
Stopping the uvicorn server instead of opening a second terminal window for curl.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item_id
steps.instructions: Add a GET '/items/{item_id}' route in main.py that takes item_id: int and returns items[item_id]. Re-create items after reload, then fetch one by index with curl.

targets.caption: Fetch an item by its index

explanations.topic: How path parameters map to function arguments
Why server reload resets the in-memory items list
Automatic type conversion from path type hints

hints: How do you capture a dynamic segment in the route path and convert it to an integer?
Use @app.get('/items/{item_id}') and annotate item_id: int in get_item.
Because saving main.py resets items[], send POST requests again before testing GET /items/0.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to re-populate items via POST after uvicorn reloads main.py.
Omitting the int type hint on item_id, which causes a TypeError when indexing the list.

steps.title: Raise 404 HTTPException for missing items
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException from fastapi and update get_item to return items[item_id] when item_id < len(items), otherwise raising a 404 HTTPException. Test requesting an out-of-range index such as /items/3.

targets.caption: Import and raise HTTPException for 404 errors

explanations.topic: Why Internal Server Error is unhelpful for missing items

hints: What happens when you request an index larger than the items list, and which HTTP status code means not found?
Import HTTPException from fastapi and check if item_id < len(items) inside get_item.
In the else branch, write raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f'Item {item_id} not found').
common_mistakes: Using return instead of raise with HTTPException.
Forgetting to import HTTPException from fastapi at the top of main.py.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint with limit parameter
steps.instructions: Add a GET '/items' route list_items accepting limit: int = 10 and returning items[0:limit]. Test it with ?limit=3 and without limit.

explanations.topic: Difference between query parameters and JSON payloads
Default query parameter values and automatic int conversion

hints: How do you define an optional query parameter with a default value in FastAPI?
Decorate def list_items(limit: int = 10): with @app.get('/items').
Return items[0:limit] and test with curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'.
common_mistakes: Forgetting quotes around the URL when passing ?limit=3 in your shell.
Giving list_items the same function name as get_item or create_item.

steps.title: Define Pydantic Item model and test
steps.instructions: Import BaseModel, define class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, and use Item in create_item and get_item. Send a JSON body via curl -d.

explanations.topic: Why Pydantic models help structure and validate data
Why modeled arguments require a JSON body instead of query params
Making fields required by removing default values

hints: How does FastAPI distinguish between a query parameter and a JSON request body?
Import BaseModel from pydantic, create class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, and update create_item(item: Item).
Send the payload using curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items'.
common_mistakes: Still passing ?item=apple in the query string after switching create_item to accept a Pydantic model.
Leaving text: str = None when you want the text field to be required.
steps.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    text: str
    is_done: bool = False

steps.title: Add response_model to GET routes
steps.instructions: Add response_model=list[Item] to the @app.get('/items') decorator and response_model=Item to @app.get('/items/{item_id}').

explanations.topic: How response_model documents and enforces response structure

hints: Which decorator argument lets you declare the response schema in FastAPI?
Pass response_model=Item to @app.get('/items/{item_id}') and response_model=list[Item] to @app.get('/items').
common_mistakes: Putting response_model inside the function parameters instead of the @app.get decorator.

steps.title: Test endpoints in interactive Swagger docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in Chrome, expand POST /items, click Try it out, and execute with a JSON body. Also inspect /redoc and /openapi.json.

explanations.topic: Alternative ReDoc UI at /redoc and OpenAPI JSON schema

hints: Where does FastAPI automatically serve interactive API documentation?
Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, expand POST /items, and click Try it out.
Edit the JSON request body and click Execute to see the curl command and response body.
common_mistakes: Testing /docs while the uvicorn server is not running.
